sampling_method: Set A candidates = every merged.json row with a key rename/duplicate/collision (27), ENTRYTYPE change, verdict ambiguous/no_source, a DOI dropped by doi_title_mismatch (Thor13, Sand80), or a title/journal/booktitle change naming a different work, edition or version (BrowMcCo06, AshbMadd98, Hint76, NormEtal08, RoedEtal98, Rayp72, LyonEtal06, Hofs01, BradLang99, Amer23c, SquiEtal04a book->chapter, Stey01/BairNoma78 swaps, and the inbook/incollection->@article conversions Dond69, Conl09, SchaRitt09, Wolf09, EnglKane04); no identity_quote_failed rows. Candidates = 95 > 60, so A = all 46 renames/duplicates/collisions/different-work cases + random.Random(20261002).sample(rest=49, 14) = 60 (14 of the 49 plain type changes and ambiguous/no_source rows; 35 not reviewed). Pool = sorted keys outside the 95 candidates (145); B = random.Random(20261002).sample(pool, round(145/3)) = 48. Every DOI re-fetched from api.crossref.org (1 req/s) or DataCite; LoC SRU (lx2.loc.gov:210) by LCCN/ISBN/title for 40+ books; Open Library for EnglKane04, Pavl27, Mill96, Murd79; local PDFs for LyonEtal06, MannEtal15; publisher/author pages for BradLang99, Amer23c, SquiEtal04a, HestEtal05, CannEtal16; IA djvu text for Herb34; HEAD cdl.bib (git show) for duplicates, collisions and house forms. FINAL merged.json values judged field by field.
systematic_findings: POST-CHECK (@inbook -> @incollection chapter move) overrides the researcher: when an @inbook has a chapter field, the rule copies the CITED chapter into title even when the researcher corrected the chapter title in `title`. GoldEtal08 ('Neural integrator models' -> cited draft 'Neural integrators: recurrent mechanisms and models'), Howa08 ('Memory: computational models' -> cited 'Computational models of working memory'), BoraEtal05 (outside the sample: researcher's serial comma lost). The merged row even labels the result source 'researcher'. Fix: when the researcher gives a confirmed/corrected title for a titled-chapter @inbook, use it as the chapter title.

POST-CHECK (same rule) swaps title and booktitle when the chapter field holds the BOOK title (Stey01: chapter 'Encyclopedia of Cognitive Science'; BairNoma78: chapter 'Fundamentals of Scaling and Psychophysics'), and it runs on a no_source row (BairNoma78) although no_source rows must not change. Result: 2 entries naming a book as the chapter. Fix: skip the move for no_source/ambiguous rows, and do not move when the researcher's notes/booktitle value say the fields are swapped (BairNoma78's researcher booktitle = the chapter field).

POST-CHECK (ambiguous rows): confirmed/corrected fields of an ambiguous verdict are applied piecemeal, producing a mixed-version entry: Ebbi85 gets the 1913 translation's title and DOI while keeping year 1885. Suggest holding all changes of an ambiguous row, or at least any DOI whose record year differs from the kept year.

POST-CHECK (duplicates within one wave): Rugg00 and RuggAlla00 are each told to merge into the other (summary.duplicates maps both ways). The earlier-key/correct-key tie-break is missing when both rows are in the same wave; RuggAlla00 (the rule-conforming key) should be kept.

POST-CHECK (keys): ChatGPT -> Open23 is renamed only because the key never followed the ID rule; the README rule renames only after a correction to year/first author/author count. Deliberate keys should be kept (or listed in key_overrides.json).

POST-CHECK (held field leaves an inconsistent entry): Herb34's address is held by the quote check (house country word 'Germany' not printed) while the year/publisher move to the 1891 Langensalza edition, leaving 'Königsberg, {RU}' with Hermann Beyer & Söhne 1891. The quote check should accept the house country suffix when the city is quoted.

POST-CHECK (DOI title check): Sand80's correct DOI 10.1016/s0166-4115(08)61955-x (Crossref pp. 331-354, 1980, A.F. Sanders, 'Tutorials in Motor Behavior') is dropped because Elsevier deposits a leading chapter number ('20 Stage Analysis of Reaction Processes'); the section-numeral rule handles 'I.—' but not a bare arabic chapter number. Thor13's 'dropped' DOI is the entry's existing DOI ('Vol 2' part label), so the flag is spurious but harmless.
